messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

function.name: look_up_scientific_contributions

message.content:
**Key Properties of Hydrogen**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Group/Period** | Group 1A (alkali metals), Period 1 |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| **Molecular weight** | 1.008 g mol⁻¹ (protium) |
| **State at room temperature** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| **Bond type** | Diatomic molecule H₂ (covalent bond) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts explosively with air or oxygen |
| **Reducing ability** | Strong reducing agent; reduces metal oxides to metals |
| **Hydrogen bonding** | Forms hydrogen bonds in water (H₂O) and other molecules |
| **Abundance** | Most abundant element in the Universe (~75 % by mass) |
| **Role in stars** | Core fusion reaction in stars produces helium from hydrogen |
| **Applications** | Fuel (liquid hydrogen, fuel cells), industrial reducing agent, laboratory reagent, cryogenic coolant, isotope labeling, etc. |

These values capture the essential physical, chemical, and astronomical characteristics that define hydrogen.
